claim: HOTAIR is a 2.2-kb long noncoding RNA (lncRNA).
source: HOTAIR is a 2.2-kb long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) whose dysregulation has been linked to oncogenesis, defects in pattern formation during early development, and irregularities during the process of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a basic characterization of HOTAIR.

claim: HOTAIR dysregulation has been linked to oncogenesis.
source: HOTAIR is a 2.2-kb long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) whose dysregulation has been linked to oncogenesis, defects in pattern formation during early development, and irregularities during the process of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT).
evidence: This claim is supported by references to prior literature establishing this connection.

claim: HOTAIR dysregulation has been linked to defects in pattern formation during early development.
source: HOTAIR is a 2.2-kb long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) whose dysregulation has been linked to oncogenesis, defects in pattern formation during early development, and irregularities during the process of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT).
evidence: This claim references established knowledge from prior research.

claim: HOTAIR dysregulation has been linked to irregularities during the process of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT).
source: HOTAIR is a 2.2-kb long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) whose dysregulation has been linked to oncogenesis, defects in pattern formation during early development, and irregularities during the process of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT).
evidence: This claim references established knowledge from prior research.

claim: Sustained high levels of HOTAIR over time increased breast metastatic capacity and invasiveness in breast cancer cells.
source: We show that sustained high levels of HOTAIR over time increased breast metastatic capacity and invasiveness in breast cancer cells, promoting migration and subsequent metastasis to the lung.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from the transgenic mouse model and in vitro assays.

claim: HOTAIR promotes migration and subsequent metastasis to the lung.
source: We show that sustained high levels of HOTAIR over time increased breast metastatic capacity and invasiveness in breast cancer cells, promoting migration and subsequent metastasis to the lung.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from tail vein injection assays and histological analysis.

claim: Withdrawal of HOTAIR overexpression reverted the metastatic phenotype.
source: Subsequent withdrawal of HOTAIR overexpression reverted the metastatic phenotype, indicating oncogenic lncRNA addiction.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from invasion assays and tail vein injection experiments after Dox withdrawal.

claim: HOTAIR exhibits oncogenic lncRNA addiction.
source: Subsequent withdrawal of HOTAIR overexpression reverted the metastatic phenotype, indicating oncogenic lncRNA addiction.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that withdrawal of HOTAIR reverses the metastatic phenotype.

claim: HOTAIR overexpression altered the cellular transcriptome of multiple metastasis-associated genes.
source: Furthermore, HOTAIR overexpression altered both the cellular transcriptome and chromatin accessibility landscape of multiple metastasis-associated genes and promoted EMT.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing differential gene expression.

claim: HOTAIR overexpression altered the chromatin accessibility landscape of multiple metastasis-associated genes.
source: Furthermore, HOTAIR overexpression altered both the cellular transcriptome and chromatin accessibility landscape of multiple metastasis-associated genes and promoted EMT.
evidence: This is supported by ATAC-seq data showing differential chromatin accessibility.

claim: HOTAIR overexpression promoted EMT.
source: Furthermore, HOTAIR overexpression altered both the cellular transcriptome and chromatin accessibility landscape of multiple metastasis-associated genes and promoted EMT.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data showing changes in EMT markers.

claim: HOTAIR-induced alterations are abrogated within several cell cycles after HOTAIR expression is reverted to basal levels.
source: These alterations are abrogated within several cell cycles after HOTAIR expression is reverted to basal levels, indicating an erasable lncRNA-associated epigenetic memory.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data showing reversal of changes after Dox withdrawal.

claim: HOTAIR exhibits an erasable lncRNA-associated epigenetic memory.
source: These alterations are abrogated within several cell cycles after HOTAIR expression is reverted to basal levels, indicating an erasable lncRNA-associated epigenetic memory.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that HOTAIR-induced changes are reversible upon withdrawal.

claim: HOTAIR has a continual role in programming a metastatic gene regulatory program.
source: These results suggest that a continual role for HOTAIR in programming a metastatic gene regulatory program.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement for ongoing HOTAIR expression to maintain the metastatic phenotype.

claim: Targeting HOTAIR lncRNA may potentially serve as a therapeutic strategy to ameliorate breast cancer progression.
source: Targeting HOTAIR lncRNA may potentially serve as a therapeutic strategy to ameliorate breast cancer progression.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the reversibility of HOTAIR-induced phenotypes.

claim: Tens of thousands of lncRNAs have been identified by high-throughput RNA sequencing.
source: Tens of thousands of lncRNAs have been identified by high-throughput RNA sequencing, but only a small percentage of these species have been functionally characterized (Cabili et al., 2011; Forrest et al., 2014; Djebali et al., 2012; Iyer et al., 2015; Vancura et al., 2021; Zhou et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Only a small percentage of identified lncRNAs have been functionally characterized.
source: Tens of thousands of lncRNAs have been identified by high-throughput RNA sequencing, but only a small percentage of these species have been functionally characterized (Cabili et al., 2011; Forrest et al., 2014; Djebali et al., 2012; Iyer et al., 2015; Vancura et al., 2021; Zhou et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Several lncRNAs serve important roles in gene regulation, including modulating gene transcription.
source: Several lncRNAs serve important roles in gene regulation, including modulating gene transcription; controlling nuclear architecture; mRNA stability, translation, and deposition of post-translational modifications (Yao et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: LncRNAs can act as molecular scaffolds to bring multiple proteins into proximity in three-dimensional space.
source: LncRNAs perform these functions through a variety of mechanisms, such as by acting as molecular scaffolds to bring multiple proteins into proximity in three-dimensional space; as 'guides' like Xist and HOTAIR which recruit chromatin-modifying enzymes to the genome; and as bridges which link promoters to distal enhancers to alter gene expression levels (Gupta et al., 2010; Lee, 2009; Rinn et al., 2007; Tsai et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Xist and HOTAIR act as 'guides' which recruit chromatin-modifying enzymes to the genome.
source: LncRNAs perform these functions through a variety of mechanisms, such as by acting as molecular scaffolds to bring multiple proteins into proximity in three-dimensional space; as 'guides' like Xist and HOTAIR which recruit chromatin-modifying enzymes to the genome; and as bridges which link promoters to distal enhancers to alter gene expression levels (Gupta et al., 2010; Lee, 2009; Rinn et al., 2007; Tsai et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Some lncRNAs act as bridges which link promoters to distal enhancers to alter gene expression levels.
source: LncRNAs perform these functions through a variety of mechanisms, such as by acting as molecular scaffolds to bring multiple proteins into proximity in three-dimensional space; as 'guides' like Xist and HOTAIR which recruit chromatin-modifying enzymes to the genome; and as bridges which link promoters to distal enhancers to alter gene expression levels (Gupta et al., 2010; Lee, 2009; Rinn et al., 2007; Tsai et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: LUNAR1 and CCAT1 facilitate or inhibit long-range chromatin interactions.
source: Some lncRNAs, such as LUNAR1 and CCAT1, facilitate or inhibit long-range chromatin interactions (Ma et al., 2015; Trimarchi et al., 2014; Xiang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The disruption of lncRNAs has been linked to the pathogenesis of human developmental defects, neuronal disorders, and cancer processes.
source: The disruption of lncRNAs has been linked to the pathogenesis of human developmental defects, neuronal disorders, and cancer processes (Fatica and Bozzoni, 2014; Huarte, 2015; Statello et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Human HOTAIR is transcribed from the HOXC locus.
source: Human HOX antisense intergenic RNA (HOTAIR) is a 2.2-kb RNA transcribed from the HOXC locus, and is expressed in posterior and distal body sites in accordance with its location within the HOX locus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HOTAIR.

claim: HOTAIR is expressed in posterior and distal body sites in accordance with its location within the HOX locus.
source: Human HOX antisense intergenic RNA (HOTAIR) is a 2.2-kb RNA transcribed from the HOXC locus, and is expressed in posterior and distal body sites in accordance with its location within the HOX locus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HOTAIR expression patterns.

claim: HOTAIR binds both Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) and LSD1 complexes.
source: HOTAIR binds both Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) and LSD1 complexes and recruits them to multiple genomic sites to promote coordinated H3K27 methylation and H3K4 demethylation, respectively, for gene silencing (Chu et al., 2011; Jarroux et al., 2021; Rinn et al., 2007; Tsai et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: HOTAIR recruits PRC2 and LSD1 complexes to multiple genomic sites to promote coordinated H3K27 methylation and H3K4 demethylation for gene silencing.
source: HOTAIR binds both Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) and LSD1 complexes and recruits them to multiple genomic sites to promote coordinated H3K27 methylation and H3K4 demethylation, respectively, for gene silencing (Chu et al., 2011; Jarroux et al., 2021; Rinn et al., 2007; Tsai et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The primary sequences of HOTAIR are poorly conserved between humans and mice.
source: Although the primary sequences of HOTAIR are poorly conserved between humans and mice, human and murine HOTAIR orthologs demonstrate some functional similarities and conserved RNA secondary structures (Li et al., 2013; Somarowthu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Human and murine HOTAIR orthologs demonstrate some functional similarities and conserved RNA secondary structures.
source: Although the primary sequences of HOTAIR are poorly conserved between humans and mice, human and murine HOTAIR orthologs demonstrate some functional similarities and conserved RNA secondary structures (Li et al., 2013; Somarowthu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The sequence divergence between human and mouse HOTAIR creates a challenge to study human HOTAIR in vivo.
source: Nonetheless, the sequence divergence creates a challenge to study human HOTAIR in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of sequence conservation.

claim: The overexpression of HOTAIR in several types of human cancers, including breast cancers has been linked to poor survival and increased metastasis.
source: The overexpression of HOTAIR in several types of human cancers, including breast cancers has been linked to poor survival and increased metastasis (Gupta et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2013; Kogo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: HOTAIR is several hundred-fold more highly expressed in metastatic breast tumors and primary breast tumors destined to metastasize.
source: Within breast cancer, HOTAIR has been found to be several hundred-fold more highly expressed in metastatic breast tumors and primary breast tumors destined to metastasize (Gupta et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: HOTAIR overexpression in primary breast cancers is a significant and independent predictor of subsequent metastasis and death across multiple independent cohorts.
source: HOTAIR overexpression in primary breast cancers is a significant and independent predictor of subsequent metastasis and death across multiple independent cohorts (Gupta et al., 2010; Sørensen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The histone methyltransferase Ezh2, a component of the PRC2 complex, can induce long-term silencing by creating a heterochromatin environment at endogenous human gene loci.
source: For example, the histone methyltransferase Ezh2, a component of the PRC2 complex, can induce long-term silencing by creating a heterochromatin environment at endogenous human gene loci (Holoch et al., 2021; O'Geen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Human HOTAIR cDNA was integrated downstream of a tetracycline response element (TRE) at the HPRT locus through inducible cassette exchange recombination in A2Lox.cre mouse embryonic stem cells.
source: Human HOTAIR cDNA was integrated downstream of a tetracycline response element (TRE) at the HPRT locus through inducible cassette exchange recombination in A2Lox.cre mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs) (Iacovino et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used to generate the transgenic model.

claim: The transcription of reverse tetracycline transactivator (rtTA) protein is stimulated by the addition of 1–2 μg/ml of Dox effector, leading to HOTAIR overexpression upon rtTA binding of TRE.
source: In this binary control system, the transcription of reverse tetracycline transactivator (rtTA) protein is stimulated by the addition of 1–2 μg/ml of Dox effector, leading to HOTAIR overexpression upon rtTA binding of TRE (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the mechanism of the inducible system and is illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: HOTAIR can be effectively induced in mESC with the addition of Dox.
source: We confirmed that HOTAIR can be effectively induced in mESC with the addition of the drug (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Upon withdrawing Dox treatment in ES cells, HOTAIR overexpression returned to baseline levels within 48 hr.
source: In addition, we validated that upon withdrawing Dox treatment in these ES cells, HOTAIR overexpression returned to baseline levels within 48 hr (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: HOTAIR-rtTA mice fed with Dox consistently expressed exponentially higher levels of HOTAIR compared to untreated control mice.
source: HOTAIR-rtTA mice fed with Dox consistently expressed exponentially higher levels of HOTAIR compared to untreated control mice, as verified through quantitative reverse transcription PCR(qRT-PCR) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: HOTAIR overexpression in mice has little effect in a normal genetic background.
source: The subtlety of these phenotypes suggests that HOTAIR overexpression in mice has little effect in a normal genetic background (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is inferred from phenotypic analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: HOTAIR transcript expression in PyMT mice containing the iHOT construct (iHOT+ Dox+ mice) was several hundred-fold higher compared to untreated iHOT mice (iHOT+ Dox− mice) or control mice which did not contain the iHOT construct (iHOT− mice).
source: We confirmed HOTAIR induction in this breast cancer model after Dox treatment using qRT-PCR, and found that HOTAIR transcript expression in PyMT mice containing the iHOT construct (iHOT+ Dox+ mice) was several hundred-fold higher compared to untreated iHOT mice (iHOT+ Dox− mice) or control mice which did not contain the iHOT construct (iHOT− mice) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Primary breast tumor weight and tumor numbers were not affected by continuous exposure to elevated levels of HOTAIR.
source: First, we found that primary breast tumor weight and tumor numbers were not affected by continuous exposure to elevated levels of HOTAIR (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Mice continually exposed to induced HOTAIR displayed a greater number of metastatic tumors and larger tumor volumes in the lungs.
source: In contrast, after subsequent dissection of lung sections and hematoxylin and eosin staining (H&E staining), we observed a greater number of metastatic tumors and larger tumor volumes in the lungs of mice continually exposed to induced HOTAIR (iHOT+ mice + Dox treatment, Figure 2D–E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), indicating that HOTAIR overexpression drives metastatic progression.
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figures 2D-E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: HOTAIR overexpression drives metastatic progression.
source: In contrast, after subsequent dissection of lung sections and hematoxylin and eosin staining (H&E staining), we observed a greater number of metastatic tumors and larger tumor volumes in the lungs of mice continually exposed to induced HOTAIR (iHOT+ mice + Dox treatment, Figure 2D–E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), indicating that HOTAIR overexpression drives metastatic progression.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of increased lung metastases in HOTAIR-overexpressing mice.

claim: Dox itself has no significant influence in tumor progression of MMTV-PyMT mice.
source: In addition, we also observed that Dox itself has no significant influence in tumor progression of MMTV-PyMT mice as previously reported (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A; Nwokafor et al., 2016; Rumney et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and citations to prior research.

claim: Expression of endogenous mouse Hotair was very low.
source: We found that expression of endogenous mouse Hotair was very low (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) and that the knockout of this gene has no significant influence on breast tumor metastasis in MMTV-PyMT mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The knockout of endogenous mouse Hotair has no significant influence on breast tumor metastasis in MMTV-PyMT mice.
source: We found that expression of endogenous mouse Hotair was very low (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) and that the knockout of this gene has no significant influence on breast tumor metastasis in MMTV-PyMT mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: High HOTAIR expression promotes breast cancer metastasis in an autochthonous cancer model with intact immune system.
source: These results demonstrate that high HOTAIR expression promotes breast cancer metastasis in an autochthonous cancer model with intact immune system, consistent with previous clinical observations in patients and studies using xenograft models.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the iHOT-PyMT mouse model.

claim: HOTAIR RNA was hundreds-fold higher expressed in iHOT+ cells after Dox treatment.
source: HOTAIR RNA was hundreds-fold higher expressed in iHOT+ cells after Dox treatment and levels quickly decreased within 24 hr after Dox withdrawal, consistent with our observations in the in vivo HOTAIR-rtTA mouse (Figures 1C and 3B).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: HOTAIR levels quickly decreased within 24 hr after Dox withdrawal in iHOT+ cells.
source: HOTAIR RNA was hundreds-fold higher expressed in iHOT+ cells after Dox treatment and levels quickly decreased within 24 hr after Dox withdrawal, consistent with our observations in the in vivo HOTAIR-rtTA mouse (Figures 1C and 3B).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: HOTAIR localizes to both the nucleus and cytoplasm in iHOT+ cells.
source: In addition, we analyzed the subcellular localization of HOTAIR in iHOT+ cells using smFISH and found HOTAIR to localize to both the nucleus and cytoplasm.
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data.

claim: The signals intensity of HOTAIR increased upon Dox treatment.
source: The signals intensity of HOTAIR increased upon Dox treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Dox-induced HOTAIR overexpression promotes increased invasive capacity in iHOT+ cells.
source: Dox-induced HOTAIR overexpression promotes increased invasive capacity in iHOT+ cells and the increased invasive capacity of these cells can be rescued when HOTAIR is restored to baseline levels after Dox withdrawal.
evidence: This is supported by Matrigel invasion assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The increased invasive capacity of iHOT+ cells can be rescued when HOTAIR is restored to baseline levels after Dox withdrawal.
source: Dox-induced HOTAIR overexpression promotes increased invasive capacity in iHOT+ cells and the increased invasive capacity of these cells can be rescued when HOTAIR is restored to baseline levels after Dox withdrawal.
evidence: This is supported by Matrigel invasion assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: HOTAIR expression levels do not affect proliferation of iHOT+ breast cancer cells.
source: We also measured the growth curve of iHOT+ cells under these same three conditions and found that HOTAIR expression levels do not affect proliferation of iHOT+ breast cancer cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by proliferation assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Mice injected with Dox-treated iHOT+ cells displayed significantly higher lung colonization after tail vein injection compared to untreated control groups.
source: As expected, mice injected with Dox-treated iHOT+ cells displayed significantly higher lung colonization after tail vein injection compared untreated control groups.
evidence: This is supported by bioluminescence imaging data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Mice injected with cells that had been treated with Dox and subsequently withdrawn displayed low lung colonization of fluorescent cells, similar to the bioluminescence profile of mice injected with untreated iHOT+ control cells.
source: Mice injected with cells that had been treated with Dox and subsequently withdrawn displayed low lung colonization of fluorescent cells, similar to the bioluminescence profile of mice injected untreated iHOT+ control cells (Figure 3D, E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by bioluminescence imaging data shown in Figures 3D-E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The increased metastatic potential of HOTAIR overexpressing breast cancer cells requires ongoing HOTAIR activity.
source: Altogether, our results suggest that the increased metastatic potential of HOTAIR overexpressing breast cancer cells requires ongoing HOTAIR activity and is abrogated by silencing HOTAIR.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that withdrawal of HOTAIR reduces metastatic potential.

claim: The increased metastatic potential of HOTAIR overexpressing breast cancer cells is abrogated by silencing HOTAIR.
source: Altogether, our results suggest that the increased metastatic potential of HOTAIR overexpressing breast cancer cells requires ongoing HOTAIR activity and is abrogated by silencing HOTAIR.
evidence: This is supported by tail vein injection and histological data.

claim: The lung sections of mice injected with HOTAIR overexpressing cells displayed a higher metastatic tumor burden compared to mice injected with HOTAIR withdrawn cells or untreated control cells.
source: The lung sections of mice injected with HOTAIR overexpressing cells displayed a higher metastatic tumor burden compared to mice injected with HOTAIR withdrawn cells or untreated control cells (Figure 3E, F).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figures 3E-F.

claim: Breast cancer cells with elevated HOTAIR require persistent and sustained HOTAIR overexpression to retain a highly invasive and metastatic phenotype.
source: In brief, we conclude that breast cancer cells with elevated HOTAIR require persistent and sustained HOTAIR overexpression to retain a highly invasive and metastatic phenotype.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement for ongoing HOTAIR expression to maintain the metastatic phenotype.

claim: There were 219 upregulated genes and 280 downregulated genes in the Dox-treated HOTAIR overexpressing group compared to the untreated control group (FDR <0.05, fold change >2).
source: RNA-seq analysis revealed that there were 219 upregulated genes and 280 downregulated genes in the Dox-treated HOTAIR overexpressing group compared to the untreated control group (FDR <0.05, fold change >2, Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: GO terms such as 'epithelial cell proliferation' and 'Wnt Signaling Pathway and Pluripotency' were enriched in the upregulated gene group.
source: We discovered that GO terms such as 'epithelial cell proliferation' and 'Wnt Signaling Pathway and Pluripotency' were enriched in the upregulated gene group, and terms such as 'regulation of cell adhesion' were enriched in the downregulated gene group.
evidence: This is supported by GO analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: GO terms such as 'regulation of cell adhesion' were enriched in the downregulated gene group.
source: We discovered that GO terms such as 'epithelial cell proliferation' and 'Wnt Signaling Pathway and Pluripotency' were enriched in the upregulated gene group, and terms such as 'regulation of cell adhesion' were enriched in the downregulated gene group.
evidence: This is supported by GO analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: Most DEGs revert to expression levels similar to that of the untreated control group in the Dox withdrawal condition.
source: Importantly, in the Dox withdrawal condition, we observed that most of these DEGs to revert to expression levels similar to that of the untreated control group.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Genes that are differentially expressed due to high levels of HOTAIR transcript in the system can be subsequently reversed to their original expression level upon HOTAIR withdrawal.
source: This result suggests that genes that are differentially expressed due to high levels of HOTAIR transcript in the system can be subsequently reversed to their original expression level upon HOTAIR withdrawal (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is inferred from RNA-seq data showing reversal of gene expression changes.

claim: The transcriptome patterns of Dox withdrawal cells are similar to Dox− cells.
source: We visualized gene expression changes between experimental groups using a hierarchical clustering heatmap, revealing that the transcriptome patterns of Dox withdrawal cells are similar to Dox− cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: There are very few DEGs (2 upregulated and 15 downregulated) when comparing DoxWD vs. Dox− groups.
source: We also compared DEGs within DoxWD vs. Dox− groups and found very few DEGs (2 upregulated and 15 downregulated).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: There is little overlap between DEGs in DoxWD vs. Dox− groups compared to DEGs between Dox+ and Dox− groups.
source: Furthermore, we observed little overlap between these DEGs compared to DEGs between Dox+ and Dox− groups (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: High levels of HOTAIR induced by Dox treatment led to altered chromatin accessibility.
source: High levels of HOTAIR induced by Dox treatment led to altered chromatin accessibility (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There are in total 1933 peaks with differential accessibility between all HOTAIR high Dox+ and all HOTAIR low Dox− cells, of which 1048 peaks are upregulated and 885 peaks are downregulated.
source: There are in total 1933 peaks with differential accessibility between all HOTAIR high Dox+ and all HOTAIR low Dox− cells, of which 1048 peaks are upregulated and 885 peaks are downregulated.
evidence: This is supported by ATAC-seq data analysis.

claim: Both up- and downregulated peaks are mainly located in distal intergenic regions (about 50%).
source: We observed both up- and downregulated peaks to be mainly located in distal intergenic regions (about 50%).
evidence: This is supported by ATAC-seq peak annotation analysis.

claim: A higher percentage of downregulated peaks occur in promoter regions less than 1 kb.
source: We found that a higher percentage of downregulated peaks occur in promoter regions less than 1 kb, indicating that HOTAIR most likely functions suppressively near promoter regions to modulate the expression of downregulated genes (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by ATAC-seq peak annotation analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: HOTAIR most likely functions suppressively near promoter regions to modulate the expression of downregulated genes.
source: We found that a higher percentage of downregulated peaks occur in promoter regions less than 1 kb, indicating that HOTAIR most likely functions suppressively near promoter regions to modulate the expression of downregulated genes (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is inferred from the enrichment of downregulated peaks in promoter regions.

claim: The top motif enriched in upregulated peaks involved many transcription factors associated with tumor metastasis, such as AP-1 family members Fra1, JunB, Atf3, and Fos.
source: The top motif enriched in upregulated peaks involved many transcription factors associated with tumor metastasis, such as AP-1 family members Fra1, JunB, Atf3, and Fos (Belguise et al., 2005; Hyakusoku et al., 2016; Milde-Langosch et al., 2004; Yuan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by HOMER motif analysis and citations to prior research.

claim: Sox7 plays inhibitory roles related to cellular proliferation, migration, and invasion in breast cancer.
source: In the top motif enriched in downregulated peaks, Sox7 was reported to play inhibitory roles related to cellular proliferation, migration, and invasion in breast cancer (Stovall et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Sox15 is a potential tumor suppressor of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
source: Previous work in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma has demonstrated that Sox15 is a potential tumor suppressor of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway (Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Cell samples subjected to Dox withdrawal clustered together with Dox− untreated control samples in a hierarchical clustering heatmap of ATAC-seq data.
source: We then analyzed peaks associated with known genes and found that cell samples subjected to Dox withdrawal also clustered together with Dox− untreated control samples in a hierarchical clustering heatmap (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There are very few differential peaks (0 upregulated and 40 downregulated) when comparing Dox− and DoxWD groups.
source: In addition, we identified very few differential peaks (0 upregulated and 40 downregulated) when comparing Dox− and DoxWD groups.
evidence: This is supported by ATAC-seq data analysis.

claim: There is little overlap between differential peaks in Dox− vs. DoxWD groups compared to differential peaks within Dox+ and Dox− groups.
source: We observed little overlap between these differential peaks compared to differential peaks within Dox+ and Dox− groups (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: This is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The chromatin accessibility level of most differential peaks identified with ATAC-seq can be subsequently rescued by HOTAIR withdrawal in the DoxWD HOTAIR low group.
source: Consistent with our previous results in our RNA-seq experiments, the chromatin accessibility level of most differential peaks identified with ATAC-seq can be subsequently rescued by HOTAIR withdrawal in the DoxWDHOTAIR low group (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: 34 upregulated genes and 58 downregulated genes are associated with differentially accessible peaks in the immediate vicinity of DEGs.
source: To further investigate downstream pathway components regulated by HOTAIR, we compared differentially accessible peaks in the immediate vicinity of DEGs, and from the overlapping set identified 34 upregulated genes and 58 downregulated genes associated with peaks.
evidence: This is supported by integrated analysis of RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data.

claim: Many of the genes with differentially accessible peaks and differential expression are linked to metastasis, such as Il33, Il34, Wnt7b, Lox, Ecm1, Col6a2 (upregulated), Kit, and Epha7 (downregulated).
source: Many of the selected genes were linked to metastasis, such as Il33, Il34, Wnt7b, Lox, Ecm1, Col6a2 (upregulated), Kit, and Epha7 (downregulated) (Figure 4E, F).
evidence: This is supported by integrated analysis of RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data shown in Figures 4E-F.

claim: Upregulated genes with differentially accessible peaks are associated with pathways such as 'connective tissue development', 'lung epithelium development', and 'regulation of leukocyte migration'.
source: GO term analysis revealed these upregulated genes are associated with pathways such as 'connective tissue development', 'lung epithelium development', and 'regulation of leukocyte migration', while downregulated genes are associated with 'cell–cell adhesion', all of which are metastasis-related cellular processes (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by GO analysis shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Downregulated genes with differentially accessible peaks are associated with 'cell–cell adhesion'.
source: GO term analysis revealed these upregulated genes are associated with pathways such as 'connective tissue development', 'lung epithelium development', and 'regulation of leukocyte migration', while downregulated genes are associated with 'cell–cell adhesion', all of which are metastasis-related cellular processes (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by GO analysis shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Il33 was upregulated with HOTAIR induction (Dox+) and reverted to low expression levels after HOTAIR withdrawal (WD).
source: As shown in examples from Figure 4H, both II33 and Wnt7b were upregulated with HOTAIR induction (Dox+) and reverted to low expression levels after HOTAIR withdrawal (WD).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq and ATAC-seq tracks shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Wnt7b was upregulated with HOTAIR induction (Dox+) and reverted to low expression levels after HOTAIR withdrawal (WD).
source: As shown in examples from Figure 4H, both II33 and Wnt7b were upregulated with HOTAIR induction (Dox+) and reverted to low expression levels after HOTAIR withdrawal (WD).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq and ATAC-seq tracks shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Kit was downregulated after HOTAIR induction and reverted to high expression levels after HOTAIR withdrawal.
source: Conversely, Kit was downregulated after HOTAIR induction and reverted to high expression levels after HOTAIR withdrawal.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq and ATAC-seq tracks shown in Figure 4H.

claim: The IL-33/ST2 signaling pathway has been linked with tumor progression, cellular invasion, and metastasis.
source: For example, ATAC-seq signals in the regulation region of the DEGs we identified display a consistent change in the ligand (Figure 4H) IL-33 and its receptor ST2, which form the IL-33/ST2 signaling pathway. This pathway has previously been linked with tumor progression, cellular invasion, and metastasis (Kim et al., 2015; Larsen et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The WNT/β-catenin pathway plays a critical role in tumorigenesis.
source: The WNT/β-catenin pathway plays a critical role in tumorigenesis, and Wnt7b was reported to function in mediating metastasis in breast cancer (Xu et al., 2020; Yeo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Wnt7b functions in mediating metastasis in breast cancer.
source: The WNT/β-catenin pathway plays a critical role in tumorigenesis, and Wnt7b was reported to function in mediating metastasis in breast cancer (Xu et al., 2020; Yeo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Kit (c-Kit, CD117, SCFR) has been reported to be involved in tumor migration or invasion.
source: Kit, also known as c-Kit, CD117 (cluster of differentiation 117), or SCFR (mast/stem cell growth factor receptor), is one of the receptor tyrosine kinases (RTK), and has been previously reported to be involved in tumor migration or invasion (Golubovskaya and Wu, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: HOTAIR transcript regulates the expression of multiple metastasis-associated genes by modifying their chromatin accessibility to promote tumor metastasis.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that HOTAIR transcript regulates the expression of multiple metastasis-associated genes by modifying their chromatin accessibility to promote tumor metastasis.
evidence: This is inferred from the integrated analysis of RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data.

claim: After Dox treatment, the mesenchymal marker Vimentin was induced and the epithelial marker E-cadherin was reduced in iHOT+ cells.
source: After Dox treatment, the mesenchymal marker Vimentin was induced and the epithelial marker E-cadherin was reduced.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: iHOT+ cells displayed more spindle-like morphology and cell detachment from epithelioid colonies after Dox treatment.
source: In addition, the iHOT+ cells also displayed more spindle-like morphology and cell detachment from epithelioid colonies (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy images shown in Figures 5A-B.

claim: When Dox was withdrawn for a brief period over three cellular passages, Vimentin was still expressed albeit at a reduced level.
source: When Dox was withdrawn for a brief period over three cellular passages, Vimentin was still expressed albeit at a reduced level.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: When Dox was withdrawn for an extended period of time over 10 cellular passages, Vimentin was largely abrogated and E-cadherin re-expressed to similar levels as in untreated cells.
source: However, when Dox was withdrawn for an extended period of time over 10 cellular passages, Vimentin was largely abrogated and E-cadherin re-expressed to similar levels as in untreated cells, and Dox withdrawn cells returned to epithelial morphology (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figures 5A-B.

claim: Dox withdrawn cells returned to epithelial morphology after extended Dox withdrawal.
source: However, when Dox was withdrawn for an extended period of time over 10 cellular passages, Vimentin was largely abrogated and E-cadherin re-expressed to similar levels as in untreated cells, and Dox withdrawn cells returned to epithelial morphology (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy images shown in Figures 5A-B.

claim: iHOT+ cells undergo EMT when exposed to HOTAIR overexpression as a result of treatment with dox.
source: These results demonstrate that iHOT+ cells undergo EMT when exposed to HOTAIR overexpression as a result of treatment with dox, and recover their original epithelial states after longer periods of withdrawal from Dox, which is consistent with the invasion and metastasis phenotypes we previously observed.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence and morphology data.

claim: iHOT+ cells recover their original epithelial states after longer periods of withdrawal from Dox.
source: These results demonstrate that iHOT+ cells undergo EMT when exposed to HOTAIR overexpression as a result of treatment with dox, and recover their original epithelial states after longer periods of withdrawal from Dox, which is consistent with the invasion and metastasis phenotypes we previously observed.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence and morphology data.

claim: Effects modulated by HOTAIR might persist for some time after HOTAIR expression is restored to basal levels.
source: However, it appears that effects modulated by HOTAIR might persist for some time.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Vimentin expression persists for several passages after Dox withdrawal.

claim: HOTAIR expression is quickly restored to basal levels within 24 hr after Dox withdrawal.
source: For example, as HOTAIR expression is quickly restored to basal levels within 24 hr after Dox withdrawal (Figure 3B), elevated Vimentin expression endures over several days lasting as long as three passages (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Elevated Vimentin expression endures over several days lasting as long as three passages after Dox withdrawal.
source: For example, as HOTAIR expression is quickly restored to basal levels within 24 hr after Dox withdrawal (Figure 3B), elevated Vimentin expression endures over several days lasting as long as three passages (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The cellular function of HOTAIR as a regulator of gene expression is conserved between mammalian lineages.
source: Collectively, our results demonstrate that the cellular function of HOTAIR as a regulator of gene expression is conserved between mammalian lineages and confirm that exposure to sustained high levels of HOTAIR over time facilitates increased EMT, invasiveness and metastatic capacity in breast cancer cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that human HOTAIR functions in mouse cells.

claim: Exposure to sustained high levels of HOTAIR over time facilitates increased EMT, invasiveness and metastatic capacity in breast cancer cells.
source: Collectively, our results demonstrate that the cellular function of HOTAIR as a regulator of gene expression is conserved between mammalian lineages and confirm that exposure to sustained high levels of HOTAIR over time facilitates increased EMT, invasiveness and metastatic capacity in breast cancer cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: Silencing HOTAIR expression for enough time abrogates the metastatic phenotype.
source: Subsequently silencing HOTAIR expression for enough time abrogates this metastatic phenotype, as well as any resulting alterations in transcriptome and chromatin accessibility, indicating that these HOTAIR-modulated alterations have not yet formed persistent epigenetic memory.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from withdrawal experiments.

claim: Silencing HOTAIR expression abrogates alterations in transcriptome and chromatin accessibility.
source: Subsequently silencing HOTAIR expression for enough time abrogates this metastatic phenotype, as well as any resulting alterations in transcriptome and chromatin accessibility, indicating that these HOTAIR-modulated alterations have not yet formed persistent epigenetic memory.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data from withdrawal experiments.

claim: HOTAIR-modulated alterations have not formed persistent epigenetic memory.
source: Subsequently silencing HOTAIR expression for enough time abrogates this metastatic phenotype, as well as any resulting alterations in transcriptome and chromatin accessibility, indicating that these HOTAIR-modulated alterations have not yet formed persistent epigenetic memory.
evidence: This is inferred from the reversibility of HOTAIR-induced changes.

claim: HOTAIR is required in an ongoing manner to reprogram oncogene expression.
source: Thus, HOTAIR is required in an ongoing manner to reprogram oncogene expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement for sustained HOTAIR expression to maintain the metastatic phenotype.

claim: Targeting overexpressed HOTAIR transcript can potentially serve as a therapeutic strategy in breast cancer patients to limit metastatic progression.
source: Our results also suggest that targeting overexpressed HOTAIR transcript can potentially serve as a therapeutic strategy in breast cancer patients to limit metastatic progression.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the reversibility of HOTAIR-induced phenotypes.

claim: Overexpression of the lncRNA HOTAIR is significantly correlated with tumor progression and poor prognosis in many kinds of tumors.
source: Overexpression of the lncRNA HOTAIR is significantly correlated with tumor progression and poor prognosis in many kinds of tumors and is a powerful predictor of tumor metastasis.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research.

claim: HOTAIR is a powerful predictor of tumor metastasis.
source: Overexpression of the lncRNA HOTAIR is significantly correlated with tumor progression and poor prognosis in many kinds of tumors and is a powerful predictor of tumor metastasis.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior research.

claim: Targeting HOTAIR overexpression is of clinical interest as a potential therapy for cancer patients.
source: As such, targeting HOTAIR overexpression is of clinical interest as a potential therapy for cancer patients (Gupta et al., 2010; Mozdarani et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The HOTAIR-rtTA-PyMT transgenic mouse provides a model to analyze the functional role of human HOTAIR in vivo within the context of breast cancer metastasis.
source: The HOTAIR-rtTA-PyMT transgenic mouse generated in this paper provides a model to analyze the functional role of human HOTAIR in vivo within the context of breast cancer metastasis.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the model generated in this study.

claim: Murine HOTAIR and human HOTAIR transcripts are conserved in structure rather than primary sequence.
source: Murine HOTAIR and human HOTAIR transcripts are conserved in structure rather than primary sequence (He et al., 2011; Yu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Human HOTAIR binds to both the PRC2 and LSD1 chromatin remodeling complexes, acting as a scaffold to target these complexes to the HOX loci and enforcing a silenced chromatin state at this position.
source: It was previously reported that human HOTAIR binds to both the PRC2 and LSD1 chromatin remodeling complexes, acting as a scaffold to target these complexes to the HOX loci and enforcing a silenced chromatin state at this position (Tsai et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Human HOTAIR may have additional gene silencing mechanisms.
source: Human HOTAIR may have additional gene silencing mechanisms (Meredith et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Murine HOTAIR has been observed to function as a trans-acting regulator similar to human HOTAIR, capable of acting in trans to influence the activities of distal genes to its site of origin.
source: Murine HOTAIR has been observed to function as a trans-acting regulator similar to human HOTAIR, capable of acting in trans to influence the activities of distal genes to its site of origin (Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Human HOTAIR transcript overexpression promotes breast cancer metastasis in vivo.
source: In our inducible human HOTAIR murine model, human HOTAIR transcript overexpression was found to promote breast cancer metastasis in vivo, consistent with previous observations in patients and human breast cancer cell lines.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the iHOT-PyMT mouse model.

claim: Human HOTAIR functions through a similar mechanism as murine HOTAIR by binding chromatin remodeling machinery and targeting the biochemical activities of these complexes to specific genomic loci.
source: Based on our ATAC-seq data, we find significant changes in the chromatin landscape when human HOTAIR is upregulated in mouse tissue, indicating that human HOTAIR functions through a similar mechanism as murine HOTAIR by binding chromatin remodeling machinery and targeting the biochemical activities of these complexes to specific genomic loci.
evidence: This is inferred from ATAC-seq data showing chromatin changes.

claim: Reprogramming of the underlying chromatin by HOTAIR leads to altered cellular function, which allows the cell to metastasize and thrive at ectopic sites.
source: We postulate that this reprogramming of the underlying chromatin by HOTAIR leads to altered cellular function, which allows the cell to metastasize and thrive at ectopic sites.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the observed data.

claim: Transcription of locus 8q24-derived oncogenic lncRNAs such as PCAT2 could recruit centromeric protein-A (CENP-A), promote the ectopic localization of CENP-A, and alter epigenetic memory at a fragile chromosomal site in human cancer cells.
source: For example, recent work showed that transcription of locus 8q24-derived oncogenic lncRNAs such as PCAT2 could recruit centromeric protein-A (CENP-A), a variant of Histone H3, promote the ectopic localization of CENP-A, and alter epigenetic memory at a fragile chromosomal site in human cancer cells (Arunkumar et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: A complete Dox withdrawal could restore all alterations in transcriptomes, chromatin states or metastatic phenotypes in iHOT+ tumor cells.
source: Our results demonstrate that a complete Dox withdrawal could restore all alterations in transcriptomes, chromatin states or metastatic phenotypes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from withdrawal experiments.

claim: The presence of HOTAIR transcript is required to promote cancer metastasis and propagate changes in the chromatin landscape.
source: Our data imply that the presence of HOTAIR transcript is required to promote cancer metastasis and propagate changes in the chromatin landscape.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement for ongoing HOTAIR expression.

claim: HOTAIR is continually needed to enforce cellular transcriptional programs—a 'lncRNA addiction'.
source: This indicates that HOTAIR is continually needed to enforce cellular transcriptional programs—a 'lncRNA addiction'.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement for ongoing HOTAIR expression.

claim: Xist lncRNA is involved in establishment of X chromosome inactivation in female cells but is largely dispensable for the maintenance of the inactive state over subsequent cell divisions and embryonic development.
source: In contrast, Xist lncRNA is involved in establishment of X chromosome inactivation in female cells but is largely dispensable for the maintenance of the inactive state over subsequent cell divisions and embryonic development (Yu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The role of HOTAIR is more akin to a transcription factor that mediates a large-scale but reversible program of gene expression.
source: In this regard, the role of HOTAIR is more akin to a transcription factor that mediates a large-scale but reversible program of gene expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the reversibility of HOTAIR-induced changes.

claim: Restoring HOTAIR expression level to baseline from a highly overexpressed state in iHOT+ breast cancer cells could rescue expression of most altered genes and chromatin accessibility.
source: We demonstrated that restoring HOTAIR expression level to baseline from a highly overexpressed state in iHOT+ breast cancer cells isolated from the primary tumors of iHOT-PyMT mice could rescue expression of most altered genes and chromatin accessibility (Figure 4A, B), as well as restoring the overall physical phenotype of the organism (Figures 3C–F–5).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and phenotypic data.

claim: Persistent and sustained HOTAIR overexpression engenders high metastatic potential within cancerous cells.
source: Our results suggest that persistent and sustained HOTAIR overexpression engender high metastatic potential within cancerous cells, further implying HOTAIR's utility as a therapeutic target.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement for ongoing HOTAIR expression to maintain metastatic phenotype.

claim: Knockdown of HOTAIR can be achieved using siRNA or ASO strategies in vitro.
source: Several studies demonstrated that knockdown of HOTAIR can be achieved using siRNA or ASO strategies in vitro (Lennox and Behlke, 2016; Rinn et al., 2007; Tsai et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2011), but targeting lncRNAs in vivo continues to present significant challenges.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A peptide nucleic acid (PNA)-based approach blocks the EZH2-binding domain of HOTAIR, inhibiting HOTAIR-EZH2 activity and subsequently decreasing invasion of ovarian and breast cancer cells and resensitizing resistant ovarian tumors to platinum-based chemotherapy.
source: A peptide nucleic acid (PNA)-based approach was reported to block the EZH2-binding domain of HOTAIR, inhibiting HOTAIR-EZH2 activity and subsequently decreasing invasion of ovarian and breast cancer cells and resensitizing resistant ovarian tumors to platinum-based chemotherapy (Özeş et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Several drugs have been recognized to indirectly downregulate HOTAIR expression.
source: In addition, several drugs have been recognized to indirectly downregulate HOTAIR expression (Mozdarani et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The isoflavone-based drugs Calycosin and Genistein inhibit HOTAIR expression by repressing Akt pathway upstream of HOTAIR transcription.
source: For example, the isoflavone-based drugs Calycosin and Genistein inhibit HOTAIR expression by repressing Akt pathway upstream of HOTAIR transcription (Chen et al., 2015; Özeş et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Direct or indirect suppression of the WNT pathway downregulates HOTAIR expression in cancer cells.
source: Direct or indirect suppression of the WNT pathway was also reported to downregulate HOTAIR expression in cancer cells (Carrion et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: There is significant overlap between HOTAIR targets and ATAC-seq differential peak-associated genes (207 genes, ~13% of ATAC-seq differential peak-associated genes).
source: We observed significant overlaps between HOTAIR targets and ATAC-seq differential peak-associated genes (207 genes, ~13% of ATAC-seq differential peak-associated genes, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by integrated analysis of ChIRP-seq and ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Among HOTAIR targets overlapping with ATAC-seq differential peak-associated genes, the chromatin accessibility of 116 genes were upregulated and 91 were downregulated.
source: Among these shared genes, the chromatin accessibility of 116 genes were upregulated and 91 were downregulated.
evidence: This is supported by integrated analysis of ChIRP-seq and ATAC-seq data.

claim: There is significant overlap between HOTAIR targets and DEGs in RNA-seq data (34 total, 13 genes were upregulated and 21 genes were downregulated in Dox+ cells compared to control).
source: We also noted significant overlap between HOTAIR targets and DEGs in our RNA-seq data (34 total, 13 genes were upregulated and 21 genes were downregulated in Dox+ cells compared to control, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by integrated analysis of ChIRP-seq and RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: 12 genes out of a total of 92 genes (~13%) which may be direct targets regulated by HOTAIR in iHOT cells were identified by comparing HOTAIR targets to genes regulated by HOTAIR through chromatin accessibility.
source: Furthermore, we compared the HOTAIR targets to genes regulated by HOTAIR through chromatin accessibility, which were represented as overlapping genes shared between our ATAC-seq and RNA-seq datasets (Figure 4E). We identified 12 genes out of a total of 92 genes (~13%) which may be direct targets regulated by HOTAIR in iHOT cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by integrated analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Almost all of the 12 potential direct HOTAIR targets were associated with migration.
source: Interestingly, almost all of these genes were associated with migration.
evidence: This is supported by literature on the functions of these genes.

claim: Genes shown to promote migration such as Ecm1, Gpr39, and Padi1 were upregulated among the potential direct HOTAIR targets.
source: Genes shown to promote migration such as Ecm1, Gpr39, and Padi1 were upregulated and genes shown to suppress migration such as Limch1 were downregulated (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by integrated analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Genes shown to suppress migration such as Limch1 were downregulated among the potential direct HOTAIR targets.
source: Genes shown to promote migration such as Ecm1, Gpr39, and Padi1 were upregulated and genes shown to suppress migration such as Limch1 were downregulated (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by integrated analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: HOTAIR regulates the expression of multiple cell adhesion- and EMT-associated genes by regulating their chromatin accessibility to promote tumor metastasis.
source: These results suggest that HOTAIR regulates the expression of multiple cell adhesion- and EMT-associated genes by regulating their chromatin accessibility to promote tumor metastasis (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is inferred from the integrated analysis of multiple datasets.

claim: HOTAIR regulates genome chromatin landscape through influencing both H3K27me3 and H3K27ac modifications.
source: Previous work showed that HOTAIR regulates genome chromatin landscape through influencing both H3K27me3 and H3K27ac modifications (Gupta et al., 2010; Jarroux et al., 2021; Song et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.
